annotations.text:
MATCHDAY — the complete MVP set.

A lit pitch, not a dark app with green paint: mown stripes, a floodlight from the top-left gantry, 2px chalk, one gold that belongs to the division and nothing else. Kit stripes are the club device in every masthead.

Six screens, one language: Pre-Season · Matchday · Sub On · Under Review · The Run · The Table.

This is the BASE — structure, language and the safety grammar. Motion, the crest, textures and the promotion moment as a real event are a later pass on top of it.

1 · PRE-SEASON — the safety screen.

Every §10 gate lives here and none of them hide. The ceiling is stated in words (0.78 kg/wk = 1% of body weight), faster paces simply aren't offered, and the copy says the engine scores your CHOSEN pace highest — not the fastest.

The band lands as a band, with the 1,500 floor named underneath.

2 · MATCHDAY — the daily driver.

612 ±100, not 512–712: one figure to act on, uncertainty stated beside it. The pitch below shows intake advancing and the band as the box you're playing into.

The day's food is the TEAM SHEET, split First Half / Second Half with subtotals.

3 · SUB ON — logging, NetDiary-grade.

Four routes in as equal peers. THE SQUAD is your regulars with appearance counts, tap to bring on; ON THE BENCH is recents with dashed numbers. Every row carries a P/C/F bar, keyed at the foot.

Quick-add by calories for when you only know the number.

4 · UNDER REVIEW — the photo check.

VAR is the right metaphor and it was sitting there: an estimate reviewed before it counts. Nothing logs until you GIVE THE DECISION.

Per-item tolerances and honest confidence — CLEAR / TIGHT / UNSIGHTED. Honey drizzle is ±34 because invisible fat is genuinely the model's blind spot; the design says so rather than hiding it. The plate is a schematic placeholder, not a stock photo.

5 · THE RUN — weight and trend.

7-day average is the headline; raw dailies are a switch that's off, with the reason next to it. The gold corridor is the pace you signed up for, so "am I on track" is a glance, not arithmetic.

Closing line keeps progress in proportion: it's 0.25 of the score. Turning up is 0.50.

6 · THE TABLE — the hero.

The breakdown is a league table: positions, weights in their own column, leader tinted gold. Consistency sits top because it IS weighted 0.50.

Survival bar shows 0.71 against the 0.65 line, +0.06 clear. The season strip is six matchweeks — the first surface that shows rank as a run.

NEXT PASS — richer visuals.

Worth doing later, on this base: a real crest/logo mark, the promotion moment as an event rather than a line, motion (the flap of a new score, the ball settling), texture on the pitch, and a proper App Store hero.

And your teams/fixtures idea. One constraint to design around: v1 shows no other user's name, number or percentile. So "teams" starts as you against your own fixture list — a season, a run, a personal best — and only becomes other people at Phase 4, if at all.
